claims.text: The baseline Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase HEA with moderate lattice distortion.
Increasing Al content while holding the other elemental fractions approximately constant increases local lattice distortion.
Increasing local lattice distortion stabilizes the single-phase solid solution.
Local lattice distortion creates a rough energy landscape for defects.
The rough energy landscape increases activation barriers for point-defect migration.
Higher point-defect migration barriers retard point-defect diffusion and long-range migration.
Retarded point-defect migration increases defect recombination rates.
Reduced defect migration and increased recombination suppress the nucleation of secondary phases and precipitates.
Reduced defect migration and increased recombination suppress the growth of secondary phases and precipitates.
Higher-Al alloys within an optimal range will retain a stable single-phase structure better than the baseline during high-temperature annealing.
Higher-Al alloys within an optimal range will develop lower densities of irradiation-induced defects than the baseline.
Higher-Al alloys within an optimal range will form fewer precipitates than the baseline under the stated extreme conditions.
The proposed microstructural stabilization will improve high-temperature strength relative to the baseline.
The proposed microstructural stabilization will improve environmental resistance relative to the baseline.
The proposed microstructural stabilization will improve radiation tolerance relative to the baseline.
The proposed microstructural stabilization will improve cryogenic toughness relative to the baseline.
The baseline alloy exhibits defect accumulation and phase segregation under harsh conditions.
Al additions beyond an optimal range may promote ordered or intermetallic phases.
Formation of ordered or intermetallic phases at excessive Al content may compromise the desired properties.
The optimal lattice-distortion threshold is sensitive to processing conditions and environmental stresses.
